title: 4. Types of input guardrails
summary: Guardrail Example --- --- Prompt injection detection Detect attempts to override instructions PII detection Identify email addresses and phone numbers Input validation Reject malformed requests Length restriction Limit extremely long prompts Topic restriction Restrict unsupported application topics Rate limiting Limit…
objectives: Explain every point in “4. Types of input guardrails” with clear language
Use the flow diagram to see what happens one step after another
Connect the visual flow to the written explanation and code

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
| Guardrail | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Prompt injection detection | Detect attempts to override instructions |
| PII detection | Identify email addresses and phone numbers |
| Input validation | Reject malformed requests |
| Length restriction | Limit extremely long prompts |
| Topic restriction | Restrict unsupported application topics |
| Rate limiting | Limit excessive request volume |
| File validation | Reject unsupported or dangerous uploads |

One important point: retrieved documents, web pages and tool outputs also need security treatment. They are not safe just because they did not come directly from the user.

steps.label: Query
steps.narration: The user query enters the system and may need rewriting before search.

steps.label: Transform
steps.narration: Query transformation expands, rewrites, or decomposes the question to improve recall.

steps.label: Search
steps.narration: Dense and/or keyword search return candidate passages.

steps.label: Fuse
steps.narration: Fusion methods such as RRF combine rankings from multiple retrievers into one list.

steps.label: Rerank
steps.narration: A cross-encoder or LLM reranker reorders candidates for higher precision context.

steps.label: Context
steps.narration: Final context is budgeted, ordered, and injected into the prompt for grounded generation.
